newsitem.title: VATICAN: Canadian priest slain in Rwanda during communion.
newsitem.headline: Canadian priest slain in Rwanda during communion.

text.p: A Canadian Roman Catholic priest was murdered while handing out communion at a mass in northern Rwanda on Sunday, the dead man's missionary order said.
The priest, 61-year-old Guy Pinard, from Trois Rivieres in Canada's Quebec province, was killed at a church in Kampanga, near the town of Ruhengeri, the White Fathers missionary order said in Rome.
Pinard's death was first announced by Pope John Paul, who told pilgrims in St Peter's Square that he had been "barbarically assassinated this morning while celebrating mass at his parish church."
"Let us pray to the Holy Virgin for him, for those who are dear to him and for his people, that they may again find peace and respect for life," the Pope said.
A spokesman for the White Fathers said Pinard had been in Rwanda since 1962. The order was seeking further details about the circumstances of the killing.
"He was killed during communion but we don't know how...We don't know if he was killed by a madman," the spokesman said.

More than half a million minority ethnic Tutsis and Hutu moderates died in 1994's Hutu-led ethnic slaughter in Rwanda, after which Tutsis swept to power and the perpetrators fled to neighbouring countries.

A new United Nations report said on Friday that Hutu death squads were killing Tutsi survivors of genocide and witnesses, who had been forced to move out of isolated areas to places near army positions and towns in search of security.

The report by the U.N. human rights office said survivors were being hunted down in their homes, intimidated, threatened and sometimes poisoned in remote areas of in the tiny central African country bordering Zaire.
The U.N. report said at least 227 genocide survivors were killed in 1996, when attacks against them rose sharply, and urged Rwanda to take measures to protect them.
Hutu militia among the 600,000 refugees who returned from Zaire late in 1996 were behind some of the attacks, the report said.
The mass influx from eastern Zaire and the expulsion of half a million Hutu refugees in Tanzania by troops in December have increased ethnic tensions in Rwanda.
